text: For a long time. <break time="0.8s" /> A terrible disease called the Red Death. <break time="0.8s" /> Had swept across the country. <break time="0.8s" /> And no plague had ever been so deadly. <break time="0.8s" /> Its mark was red. <break time="0.8s" /> For scarlet spots on the face showed. <break time="0.8s" /> That a person had caught it. <break time="0.8s" /> The whole illness. <break time="0.8s" /> From the first signs to the end. <break time="0.8s" /> Took only half an hour. <break time="0.8s" /> And no one could help the sick. <break time="0.8s" /> But Prince Prospero. <break time="0.8s" /> The ruler of the land. <break time="0.8s" /> Was happy and fearless. <break time="0.8s" /> And he was also clever. <break time="0.8s" /> In his own way. <break time="0.8s" /> When half of his people had died. <break time="0.8s" /> He invited a thousand healthy, cheerful friends. <break time="0.8s" /> From among his knights and ladies. <break time="0.8s" /> With them. <break time="0.8s" /> He went away to one of his castles. <break time="0.8s" /> A huge and magnificent building. <break time="0.8s" /> Surrounded by a strong, high wall. <break time="0.8s" /> The gates were made of iron. <break time="0.8s" /> And the courtiers sealed the bolts. <break time="0.8s" /> With fire and heavy hammers. <break time="0.8s" /> So that no one could get in or out. <break time="0.8s" /> There was plenty of food inside. <break time="0.8s" /> And the prince believed. <break time="0.8s" /> That the world outside could take care of itself. <break time="0.8s" /> He had brought clowns, dancers, musicians. <break time="0.8s" /> Beauty, and wine. <break time="0.8s" /> And it seemed foolish. <break time="0.8s" /> To feel sad or even to think. <break time="0.8s" /> Inside the walls there was safety. <break time="0.8s" /> But outside them was the Red Death.
